title: Orthrus - dual-loop system-technology co-optimization using Bayesian optimization and differential evolution
problem: System-technology co-optimization requires simultaneous optimization of algorithmic parameters, system architecture, and semiconductor technology choices. Exploring this massive multi-dimensional space is computationally expensive.
motivation: Combining multiple optimization algorithms (Bayesian optimization for sample-efficient exploration and differential evolution for global search) in a dual-loop structure can efficiently navigate complex co-optimization landscapes.
method: Orthrus uses a dual-loop optimization framework integrating Bayesian optimization for refined parameter search and differential evolution for global exploration, enabling simultaneous tuning of application, architecture, and technology parameters.
key_novelty: Dual-loop system-technology co-optimization combining Bayesian optimization and differential evolution for efficient multi-dimensional parameter space exploration.
contributions: Dual-loop co-optimization framework combining Bayesian optimization and differential evolution
Methodology for efficient system-technology design space exploration
Optimization techniques for complex interdependent design parameters
limitations: Specific performance improvements and convergence guarantees for the dual-loop approach are not detailed, limiting assessment of practical effectiveness.
